declaration.intent: Witness CHANGELOG.md and codify its discipline: append-only, Good/Bad/Ugly per entry, a 0-10 rating scale kept deliberately clear of the Leighton Weight's 0.00-2.00 range, and mandatory even when a phase went smoothly. Pair with forge-stack/docs/roadmap-process-v1, which makes a changelog entry a required step of closing any roadmap phase.

entry_format.scale_rule: 0-10, never 0.00-2.00 — that range is reserved for the Leighton Weight (λ) and must never be reused for anything else, including changelog self-assessment, to avoid a reader mistaking a confidence rating for a trust score.
entry_format.mandatory_even_when_clean: An entry with nothing to report under Bad or Ugly still states that plainly ('No bad items. <one sentence why>') rather than being omitted. A phase is not exempt from a changelog entry because it went well.

append_only_discipline.rule: Once an entry is written, it is never edited to change what it originally said. A correction is a new, later entry that says what was wrong and what the true state is — the same principle as the ledger's own append-only chain.
append_only_discipline.duplicate_or_error_handling: If an entry needs to be removed (an exact duplicate from a bad bulk-edit, for example), the removal itself is recorded in a new entry naming what was removed and why — never a silent deletion.
append_only_discipline.ordering: Entries run oldest-first, version-ordered, so the file reads as the build's actual journey rather than a reverse-chronological release log. A header note at the top of the file states this and flags any entries whose original recorded timestamp is known-unreliable — version order is authoritative over any such timestamp.

parameters.relationship_to_roadmap: Every roadmap phase's completion, per forge-stack/docs/roadmap-process-v1, ends with a changelog entry. The changelog is therefore the definitive record of what has actually shipped; ROADMAP.md should never disagree with it about whether something is done.
parameters.ai_assisted_disclosure: The changelog documents an AI-assisted build: architecture, decisions, and verification are James's; implementation velocity comes from working alongside AI. This is stated once, in the file's header note, not re-asserted per entry.
